deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page sets out a 'second method' for computing the 'Decident'. That is a lattice-point count over integer pairs (x,Y) and (Y,y). The points are taken in half-open regions such as 0 <= xi=(Ax+bY)/alpha <= 1/2 and 0 <= eta=(-Bx+aY)/alpha <= 1/2. The counted points are split into two classes by the parity of [X], Y and [y]. This is Gauss's lattice-point (Gauss-lemma type) attack on the biquadratic or Gaussian-integer character problem, built from a substitution with entries a,b,A,B,alpha,beta (and D,d). Such counts are only exact up to boundary and edge terms. Those terms depend only on the signs of the parameters.

This page (f.18r) is a sign-case table that computes those correction terms.
- Header rows: the sign pair of (a,b) in 4 blocks; the sign pair of (A,B), cycling through +-, --, -+, ++ in 16 columns; and in each column two sub-columns with the sign pair of (alpha,beta). The label reads 'alpha delta' but is probably alpha beta, as on the next page.
- Why only 32 cases: only 2 of the 4 (alpha,beta) sign pairs occur per (a,b,A,B) case. My inference is that a determinant or orientation condition removes the other two, giving 32 rather than 64 cases.
- Body rows: for each case Gauss enters the contributions of four auxiliary counts, labelled R' (or a corrected label), R'', R''' and R^0. Each is a column of small integers 0, +-1, +-2, apparently one entry per partial count.
- Last row: four-entry sums per column, e.g. 0+4 0 0, +2-2 0 0, -2-2 0 0, -2-0+2 0. These are column totals of the corrections.

Lower right: Gauss tries to express the R^0 corrections as linear combinations of sign-symbols.
- Under labels I, II, III, IV he writes terms like -1/2(Jm), -1/2(JMi^n), +1/2(Jmi^n), 1/2(JM).
- He combines them into roughly -2Jm+2JM+2Jmu.

Lower half: more small +-0, +-2, +-4, +-6 tables. These look like repeated case checks, for instance with the roles of the parameters permuted.

Next page: the outcome of this tabulation, written as closed formulas. Here (x) denotes sgn(x). For example k' = -1/2(a) - 1/2(b) and K' = -1/2(A) + 1/2(B). The general shape is R' = -1/2(a) - 1/2(b) - 1/2(A) + 1/2(B) + (alpha) + 1/2(alpha beta) + 1/2(AB ab alpha beta), and similarly for R'' and R'''.

So the page is the empirical case-by-case data from which Gauss reads off sign-indicator formulas for the boundary terms of his lattice-point count.

My reasoning on the margin note of the previous page: class I means all three or exactly one of the conditions 'Y even, [X] even, [y] even' hold. That means 0 or 2 of the quantities are odd, which is equivalent to the sum Y+[X]+[y] being even. This agrees with Gauss's marginal 'I wo [Y+x+y] gerade'.
errors: Most individual table entries cannot be verified from the image, so I cannot check them case by case.
The k' and K' rows of the next page are consistent with the closed formulas -(sgn a+sgn b)/2 and (-sgn A+sgn B)/2.

The kappa' row on the next page (values +1/2, -1/2, -3/2?, +2/2?) does not obviously match the alpha/beta part of the R' formula without knowing the sign of the S(AB ab alpha beta) term. Either the transcription or Gauss's entry is uncertain there.
Several cells were overwritten or blotted (the heavy ink in the right-hand columns of the R', R'' and R^0 rows). This indicates Gauss corrected values; no definite error can be identified.

results.what: Exhaustive sign-case tabulation of boundary/edge correction terms in a lattice-point count for a quartic (Gaussian-integer) character, with each case's corrections summed
results.modern_name: Boundary-term analysis in lattice-point (Gauss/Eisenstein-lemma type) proofs of reciprocity laws
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (lattice-point idea, 3rd/5th proofs of quadratic reciprocity); Eisenstein (geometric version, 1844); for quartic reciprocity Eisenstein and Jacobi (1844)

results.what: Expressing the correction terms as linear combinations of sign indicators sgn(a), sgn(b), sgn(A), sgn(B), sgn(alpha), sgn(alpha beta), etc. (results stated on the next page)
results.modern_name: Sign-function (indicator) decomposition of case-dependent correction terms

results.what: Parity classification: 'all three or exactly one of the even-conditions hold' is equivalent to 'the sum Y+[X]+[y] is even'

deep.surprise_reason: This is working data for Gauss's known but unpublished lattice-point approach to biquadratic residues and reciprocity. The method fits his published lattice-point proofs, and fragments on biquadratic residues appear in Werke II. The page is careful case-checking rather than a new theorem, though it documents the detail of his unpublished attempt.
